exposure: short cervical length in the early third trimester (≤25 mm)
cohort: The study included women with normal cervical length in the second trimester (16+0 to 27+6 weeks) who also had cervical length measured in the early third trimester (28+0 to 33+6 weeks), excluding those with multiple pregnancies, cerclage operation, or iatrogenic preterm birth.
finding: A short cervical length (≤25 mm) in the early third trimester significantly increased the risk of preterm birth in women with normal mid-trimester cervical length.
gest_age: Cervical length measurements were taken between 16+0 and 27+6 weeks (second trimester) and between 28+0 and 33+6 weeks (early third trimester); preterm birth was defined as birth occurring before 37 weeks of gestation.
